chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from Zurara from al-Yasa' who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no divorce according to the Sunnah except upon a state of purity from non-coitus, and no divorce according to the Sunnah and upon a state of purity from non-coitus except with a witness, and if a man divorces [his wife] according to the Sunnah and upon a state of purity from non-coitus and calls a witness and does not intend the divorce, his divorce is not a divorce.'
And conditional divorce is also not effective; what indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.طُهْر: Purity (state of being free from menses/post-natal bleeding)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam establishes the rigorous conditions for a valid Sunnah divorce, emphasizing that it must occur during a period of purity (tuhr) free from sexual intercourse and witnessed by two just individuals. It further clarifies the role of intention (niyyah), noting that mere pronunciation without the specific intent to divorce renders the act ineffective, while conditional divorce (talaq bi-shart) is also deemed invalid, reflecting the Shia juristic preference for simplicity and certainty in marital dissolution.
